etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English illuminaten, borrowed from Latin illūminātum, supine of illūminō (“lighten, light up, show off”), from in + lūminō (“light up”), from lūmen (“light”). Cognate with Old English lȳman (“to glow, shine”). More at leam.

quote.citation: 1886 October – 1887 January, H[enry] Rider Haggard, She: A History of Adventure, London: Longmans, Green, and Co., published 1887, →OCLC:
quote.text: Nero illuminated his gardens with live Christians soaked in tar, and we were now treated to a similar spectacle, probably for the first time since his day, only happily our lamps were not living ones.

quote.citation: 2006, Michael Grecco, Lighting and the Dramatic Portrait, Amphoto Books, →ISBN, page 40:
quote.text: A light that is one foot away from the subject's face will completely illuminate the face, but leave the rest of the body softer and darker.

definitions.definition: (transitive, figurative) To clarify or make something understandable.

quote.citation: 1984 December 8, Ellen Grabiner, “A Candid Portrait of Choosing Children”, in Gay Community News, volume 12, number 21, page 10:
quote.text: Jan and Maidi, a lesbian couple, do a very funny routine illuminating the simplicity of the alternative fertilization process and even go so far as to recommend the most suitable receptacles for the semen: marinated artichoke heart jars.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To decorate the page of a manuscript book with ornamental designs.

quote.citation: 2012 June 2, Phil McNulty, “England 1-0 Belgium”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: Hodgson's approach may not illuminate proceedings in Poland and Ukraine but early evidence suggests they will be tough to break down.

quote.citation: 1994, Sylvia Carlson, Verne Carlson, Professional Cameraman's Handbook, →ISBN, page 494:
quote.text: Red diode in button illuminates when camera runs at speed set in five-digit speed selector.

quote.citation: 2011/2012, "Spectrum", written by Florence Welch and Paul Epworth, performed by Florence and the Machine, released on the album Ceremonials (2011):
quote.text: Say my name / and every color illuminates. / We are shining /  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive, military) To direct a radar beam toward.
Someone thought to have an unusual degree of enlightenment.
